memoryText: And they devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Acts 2:42 slowly, several times, and say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Luke gives this single verse as a portrait of the first church after Pentecost. It is a pattern for every church that follows.

“They devoted themselves.” The verb means to persist, to be strongly committed. It was not casual. These believers made time for each other and for the means of grace.

“To the apostles” teaching.’ Their life was built on the teaching handed down from Jesus through his apostles. Today we have that teaching in the New Testament. A healthy church listens to Scripture.

“And the fellowship.” The Greek word is koinonia, sharing in common. The church is a family, bound by the same Lord and the same Spirit, sharing life and burdens.

“The breaking of bread.” This includes common meals and the Lord’s Supper, where believers remember Jesus’ death and feed on him by faith.

“And the prayers.” They prayed together, often and earnestly. The church began with prayer and moved forward in prayer.

When you wonder what the Christian life should look like, say this verse. It is simple, and it is enough to start.
weekInReview: This week you began Acts with the risen Jesus’ promise: “You will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses.” Your first doctrinal pause was on Christ’s ascension, reigning and interceding. Then you studied the person of the Holy Spirit, and saw Jesus’ promise of a Helper fulfilled at Pentecost. A pause on repentance showed you the difference between godly grief and worldly grief. Another on the means of grace showed you the ordinary ways God feeds his people: Word, sacrament, prayer, and fellowship. In Acts 2 you read Peter’s first sermon, heard three thousand respond, and saw the birth of the church.
reflectionQuestions: Jesus ascended and now reigns at the Father’s right hand. How does knowing that he is on the throne and interceding for you change the way you face this week?
Peter’s hearers were cut to the heart and asked, “What shall we do?” When have you been cut to the heart by the Spirit? How did you respond?
Of the four things the first church devoted itself to (teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, prayers), which do you most need to grow in?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for ascending and pouring out the Spirit.
Thank him for the church built at Pentecost.
